subject: Private gateway: fragmented packets and intermittent upload failures
messages:
From: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@cartographer.io>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent upload failures after gateway patch

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing intermittent large-file upload failures from our on-prem app to S3 over the private gateway after your team applied the April gateway patch (release 1.9.4) early this morning. The failures look like TCP resets and occasional 0-byte responses; short flows succeed. Attached is a short pcap taken from our edge appliance during one failure window.

Observations: 
- Failures correlate with large (>1400B) packets.
- Wireshark shows both fragmentation and TCP checksum offload mismatch flags on some packets.
- After we forced MSS clamp to 1300 on our app side, retries succeeded for ~60% of flows but not all.

Can your team help triage routing / NAT / SG interactions on the private gateway? We’re currently in a staging-to-prod cutover and are blocked.

Thanks,
Samantha
Network Ops
Cartographer Inc.
Attachment: capture_snippet.pcap (pcap, 1.1MB)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@cartographer.io>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent upload failures after gateway patch

Folks — forwarding an urgent report from Cartographer. Staging cutover experiencing intermittent failures; external netops already tried an MSS clamp. They see fragmented packets and possible checksum offload mismatches.

Immediate asks:
- Can infra confirm whether the April gateway patch touched fragmentation/DF handling or changed any TCP offload settings on GRE/GW path?
- Can we validate conntrack/NAT behavior for large (>1400B) flows and any security-group handling of fragmented fragments?
- If we need a quick mitigation, suggest an experiment (MSS clamp, MTU clamp on gateway, temporary SG accept for fragments).

I’m on standby to coordinate with Cartographer.
-V

--Original message--

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@cartographer.io>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent upload failures after gateway patch

Thanks for the ping — looked at the gateway release notes and the node configs. The patch did add a NIC driver update that changes GRO/GSO default behavior on the GW host (we rolled back the previously forced GRO disable). That can cause checksum offload mismatches when middleboxes re-fragment.

Quick findings from Cartographer pcap (attached):
- I see fragments with inconsistent checksums and a handful of packets with MF=1 where the inner packet length shows non-standard alignment.
- conntrack count spikes when these flows start; NAT entries time out after retries and we see sporadic resets.

Attachments: brief pcap excerpt and a small gw-config-diff showing the driver flag changes (gw-config-diff.txt).

Short mitigation suggestion (for immediate trial):
1) On the affected gateway nodes, disable GSO/GRO (ethtool --offload) to force kernel-side segmentation.
2) Ensure MTU clamp to 1400 on the GRE/encap interfaces (we can try 1380 if needed).
3) Temporarily allow fragmented packets through SG for the Cartographer staging CIDR for the next 6 hours while we validate.

I’ll coordinate the node-level change windows — need a thumbs up from Marissa for cluster-level rollout and Monica for SG exception.

-rishi

Attachment: capture_snippet.pcap (excerpt), gw-config-diff.txt

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@cartographer.io>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent upload failures after gateway patch

Agree with Rishi’s plan. Adding a quick playbook and rollback steps so we can run with minimal customer impact:

Playbook (30–90 minute window):
- Step 0: Notify Cartographer and CS that we’ll run a rolling change across 4 GW nodes (staging first).
- Step 1: On node-02 (staging), disable GSO/GRO: ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off. Restart netstack (no host reboot).
- Step 2: Set encap interface MTU to 1400 and add iptables raw table rule to bypass conntrack for established uploads for test CIDR.
- Step 3: Monitor conntrack metrics, NAT table sizes, and upload success rate.
- Step 4: If >90% improvement within 15 minutes, roll to node-01/03/04.
- Rollback: re-enable GSO/GRO and revert MTU/iptables if errors increase or new failure modes observed.

Security note: allowing fragments through SG is high-risk for a long window; prefer the iptables raw bypass for the short experiment and have Monica scope a very narrow SG change if needed.

Marissa — should we schedule the staging change at 13:00 PT?

-karthik

From: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@cartographer.io>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent upload failures after gateway patch

Thanks — we ran the staging test at 13:00 PT on node-02 as suggested. Results:
- After disabling GRO/GSO and clamping MTU to 1400 on the GW node, upload success rate improved from ~40% to ~95% for the staging CIDR within 10 minutes.
- A few flows still failed; the packet captures show fragments being dropped at a downstream firewall that enforces "no fragments" by default. We attached an SG audit extract (sg-audit.csv) showing the rule.

Next steps we request:
- Monica: Can your team scope a narrow SG exception to allow fragmented traffic originating from our staging CIDR for the next 2 hours while we finish validation?
- Redwood: If SG change is unacceptable, we need a longer-term fix (avoid reintroducing enabling of GSO/GRO in the gateway build or add an explicit reassembly/defragmentation step in the GW path).

We appreciate the fast triage. Happy to provide more pcaps.

—Samantha

Attachment: sg-audit.csv

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@cartographer.io>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 17:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent upload failures after gateway patch

Summary and action items:
- What we changed: disabled GSO/GRO on the staging GW node and clamped encap MTU to 1400. Immediate improvement to upload success.
- Remaining blocker: downstream SG is dropping fragments. Monica to scope a timeboxed SG exception for Cartographer staging CIDR (2 hours) to confirm end-to-end.
- Medium-term: Rishi + Karthik to propose a permanent gateway hardening plan (either keep GSO/GRO off in the release or add defragmentation on the GW path) and ship in 1.9.5.
- Monica: please confirm SG exception window and include rollback criteria (monitor for anomalous fragmented traffic pattern).
- Samantha: please continue to send pcaps for any failed flows; we’ll keep a close watch during the staging cutover.

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. I’ll open a follow-up RFC for the GW release decision once Rishi and Karthik have a recommendation.

-Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Manager, Cloud Networking
Redwood Inference
